correctness.rationale: For every n and j>=2, condition on final descendant count: arrivals to that subtree choose the parent uniformly within it, giving the exact conditional Bernoulli sum for degree. The independent beta-binomial/Pólya formula gives a strong upper size tail. Exponential Markov bounds imply that, among labels at most n^(mu+delta), a child count at least (c-eta) log n forces subtree size >n^(c/2-epsilon) whp, because the explicit rate I(c,c/2)=mu and increases under a smaller subtree. Published maximum-degree and all-maximizers label asymptotics complete the two-sided proof. Exact exhaustive computations checked all 210 joint probabilities on every RRT of orders 2 through 8. No finite computation is offered as proof of the n->infinity statement.

value.rationale: Eslava López Ortiz explicitly ask about the number of vertices removed in the first maximum-degree-targeted cut; the exact logarithmic exponent is a natural nontrivial leading-order answer for network resilience. The coupling of extreme child-count selection with descendant mass is a genuine joint extreme-value question, not an automatic fixed-label tree identity. It rigorously quantifies initial removal size while leaving full distributions and later deletions open.
